paragraph:
# Velmoria's map

*One hundred and forty-five years on, an attempt to (gerrymander) the republic tests the integrity of its (secular) institutions*

LET THIS chapter turn on a (particular) danger: the quiet corruption of a map. One hundred and forty-five years after the marshal fell, Velmoria undertook a routine task—the redrawing of electoral boundaries after a new census. It should have been a (sober), technical exercise for a (cartographer) and the keeper of the national (gazetteer). Instead it became an attempt to (gerrymander) the republic, and a (spectacular) test of whether its (secular) institutions could (decipher) and defeat the scheme.

The plot was no (oracular) mystery, but it was cleverly hidden—a (cipher) buried in the (vernacular) of bureaucratic detail. A faction in parliament, the (titular) defenders of "fair representation," sought to (render) the boundaries in their own favour: to pack rivals into a single district and dilute them across others, to (mar) the (circular) wholeness of one-citizen-one-vote—each ballot a perfect round, equal to every other—with carefully (angular) lines. Their map was a (perpendicular) absurdity, districts shaped like a stranded (caterpillar) or a broken (molar), drawn not by geography but by ambition.

The scheme came to light through a (freelancer)—a young (cartographer) of no (particular) standing, hired to (render) the official map. Studying the proposed boundaries with an (ocular) precision the plotters had not anticipated, she began to (decipher) their true purpose. The lines did not follow the river or the (conifer)-clad ridge or the path of the (aquifer); they followed the voting records. It was a (gerrymander) dressed in the (veneer) of neutrality. She would not (defer) to her employers' wishes; she took her findings to the press.

Recall how the marshal had handled elections. He did not bother to (gerrymander); he (squander)ed no breath on the pretence. He would (render) any result he pleased, (encipher) the true count and publish a (forger)'s fiction. His "elections" were a (circular) farce, a (titular) ritual with no substance. He kept a (coffer) of bribes for the compliant and what amounted to a (larder) of threats for the rest. Any (mutineer) who questioned the tally was branded a (racketeer) and made to (surrender) his freedom. The marshal's map of power had only one (pillar): himself.

The republic, (chasten)ed by that memory, refused to let the (gerrymander) stand. The (freelancer)'s revelation set off a (spectacular) public reckoning. The faction's (titular) leaders blustered and (pander)ed, deploying every (jocular) deflection and (avuncular) reassurance. They tried to (cumber) the inquiry with paperwork, to (encumber) the courts with delay, to (hinder) the (cartographer) with threats to her livelihood. One (versemonger) of a spokesman, fond of slogans masquerading as wisdom, spun (oracular) nonsense about "communities of interest"; another, a practised (faultfinder), sought to (mar) the (freelancer)'s reputation. It was a (sheer) (veneer) of legitimacy over a (vascular) rot.

The republic's institutions held. An independent boundary commission—staffed by a sober (cartographer), a meticulous compiler of the national (gazetteer), and a (lexicographer) brought in to (decipher) the slippery (vernacular) of the proposal—took up the case. They would not (defer), (malinger), or (pander). They examined every (angular) line and (perpendicular) jog, every (circular) justification, and laid the (gerrymander) bare. The map, they ruled, was a (forger)'s work—an attempt to (render) the people's will into a (cipher) only the plotters could read.

The (rejoinder) from the public was swift and (sober). Citizens who had grown comfortable—a little (insular), a little prone to (slumber)—woke to the danger. They saw in the (gerrymander) a (harbinger) of worse: the slow (vascular) constriction of democracy from within. A (bellwether) district, long a (particular) prize for the plotters, turned out in force to (steer) the republic back toward fair lines. The attempt to (gerrymander) became, by an irony the plotters could not (decipher), the very (reminder) that re-engaged a drowsy electorate.

The remedy was procedural, not vengeful. The republic did not (surrender) to the temptation of (retribution); it did not jail the plotters or (render) them outcasts. It simply struck down the corrupt map and entrenched a new rule: that boundaries would henceforth be drawn by an independent body, beyond the reach of any faction's (coffer). The (gerrymander) was undone; the (remainder) of the plotters' careers withered in the daylight. The (forger)'s map went into the archive as a (memento)—a (tinder)-dry warning of how easily the clean (circular) geometry of fair voting can be (mar)red.

Beyond the political (imbroglio), ordinary life kept its (limber), (meander)ing pace. A (forager) gathered a (tuber) and wild (nectar) in the (conifer) woods; a (bather) swam in the cool (aquifer)-fed spring; a (badger) and a (caterpillar) shared the hedgerow with a curious (gander). At the market, a vendor stirred soup in a (mortar) and strained it through a (colander); a craftsman bent (timber) and (solder)ed a (cylinder) of copper; a (ranger) rolled a (boulder) from the mountain path. The (crepuscular) light caught the (polar) glint of frost on a (girder); a (pitcher) of (ginger) beer passed from (shoulder) to (shoulder); an old (archer) taught a child to (steer) an arrow true. There was no (ulcer) of fear in the public body, only the steady (vascular) pulse of a free people.

The episode entered the national (canon) as a (particular) kind of lesson. A republic, the historians wrote, is not only menaced by the (spectacular) (coup) or the (oracular) demagogue; it can be hollowed by the quiet (gerrymander), the (cipher) in the map, the (forger)'s line drawn while the citizens (slumber). The price of liberty is an (ocular), even (auricular), vigilance—the willingness to (decipher) the (vernacular) of power and to (infer), from a (caterpillar)-shaped district, the (vascular) threat beneath. To (defer) such scrutiny, or to (malinger) in civic duty, is to invite the slow (surrender) of self-rule.

So Velmoria, one hundred and forty-five years free, learns that the integrity of a democracy lives in its least (spectacular) details—the honest line on a map, the (sober) work of a (cartographer) who refuses to (forge), the (rejoinder) of a public that will not (slumber). The marshal ruled by the (cipher) and the (forger)'s pen, by the (gerrymander) of truth itself; his country, a century and a half past his fall, has chosen the harder (vernacular) of fairness—to draw its (circular) lines by geography and not by greed, to (decipher) every (oracular) deception, and to keep, beneath the (secular) (pillar)s of its institutions, the one (particular) (reminder) that no map, however cleverly drawn, can long (encumber) a people determined to (steer) their own course.
translation:
韦尔莫利亚的地图

*历一百四十五年，一桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）这个共和国的图谋，考验着它（世俗的/secular）制度的廉正*

让这一章围绕一个（特定具体的/particular）危险展开：对一张地图悄无声息的腐蚀。元帅倒台一百四十五年后，韦尔莫利亚着手一桩例行任务——在一次新的人口普查之后重划选区边界。这本该是一桩供（制图师/cartographer）和国家（地名词典/gazetteer）保管人去做的、（持重冷静的/sober）技术性活计。然而它却变成了一桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）这个共和国的企图、和一场考验它（世俗的/secular）制度能否（破解/decipher）并挫败这一阴谋的（壮观惊人的/spectacular）测验。

这阴谋不是什么（神谕般晦涩的/oracular）谜团，但它被巧妙地藏了起来——一段埋在官僚细节那（行话土话/vernacular）里的（密码暗语/cipher)。议会里一个派系，"公平代表权"的（名义上的/titular）捍卫者，企图把边界（绘制呈现/render）成对他们自己有利：把对手挤进单单一个选区、又把他们稀释分散到另外几个选区，用精心设计的（带棱角的/angular）线条去（损毁/mar）一人一票那（圆满周正的/circular）完整——每一张选票都是一个完美的圆、与每一张别的选票相等。他们的地图是一桩（直角般生硬的/perpendicular）荒唐之物，选区形状像一条搁浅的（毛毛虫/caterpillar）或一颗断裂的（臼齿/molar)，不是按地理、而是按野心划成的。

这阴谋经由一个（自由职业者/freelancer）而曝光——一位无（特定/particular）地位的年轻（制图师/cartographer)，受雇去（绘制/render）那张官方地图。她以阴谋者们未曾料到的（目力眼睛般的/ocular）精确研究那些拟定的边界，开始（破解/decipher）他们的真实意图。那些线条不沿着河流、不沿着（针叶树/conifer）覆盖的山脊、也不沿着（含水层/aquifer）的走向；它们沿着投票记录。这是一桩裹着中立（虚饰表层/veneer）的（操纵选区划分/gerrymander)。她不肯（顺从屈从/defer）于她雇主的意愿；她把她的发现带去了新闻界。

回想元帅当年是如何处置选举的。他懒得去（操纵选区划分/gerrymander)；他不在这种伪装上（白费浪费/squander）半口气。他会（绘制炮制/render）任何他高兴的结果、把真实的计票（加密编码/encipher）起来、并刊布一份（伪造者/forger）的虚构。他的"选举"是一场（循环往复的/circular）闹剧、一种没有实质的（名义上的/titular）仪式。他给顺从者备着一（钱柜/coffer）贿赂、给其余人备着相当于一（食品储藏室/larder）的威胁。任何质疑计票的（哗变者/mutineer)，都被打上（敲诈勒索者/racketeer）的烙印，并被迫（交出/surrender）他的自由。元帅那张权力地图只有一根（支柱/pillar)：他自己。

这个共和国，被那段记忆所（惩戒警醒/chasten)，拒绝让这桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）成立。这（自由职业者/freelancer）的揭露引发了一场（壮观惊人的/spectacular）公众清算。这派系的（名义上的/titular）首脑们虚张声势、（迎合讨好/pander)，施展每一句（戏谑逗趣的/jocular）搪塞和每一句（叔伯般和蔼的/avuncular）宽慰。他们企图用文书工作来（拖累阻塞/cumber）这项调查、用拖延来（拖累阻碍/encumber）法庭、用威胁她生计来（阻碍/hinder）这位（制图师/cartographer)。一个（凑韵打油的/versemonger）发言人，钟爱乔装成智慧的口号，编造着关于"利益共同体"的（神谕般晦涩的/oracular）胡话；另一个，一个老练的（吹毛求疵者/faultfinder)，企图（损毁/mar）这（自由职业者/freelancer）的名声。这是覆在一处（血管脉络般的/vascular）腐烂之上、一层（纯然彻底的/sheer）合法性（虚饰表层/veneer)。

这个共和国的种种制度守住了。一个独立的边界委员会——由一位持重的（制图师/cartographer)、一位一丝不苟的国家（地名词典/gazetteer）编纂者、以及一位被请来（破解/decipher）这份提案那滑头（行话/vernacular）的（词典编纂者/lexicographer）所组成——接手了这桩案子。他们不会（顺从屈从/defer）、（装病偷懒/malinger）、或（迎合讨好/pander)。他们审查每一条（带棱角的/angular）线和每一处（直角般生硬的/perpendicular）拐折、每一条（循环往复的/circular）辩白，并把这桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）和盘托出。他们裁定，这张地图是一个（伪造者/forger）的勾当——一桩把人民的意志（绘制炮制/render）成一段只有阴谋者才能读懂之（密码/cipher）的企图。

公众的（反驳回应/rejoinder）迅速而（持重冷静/sober)。那些已变得安逸——有点（孤立闭塞/insular)、有点容易（沉睡/slumber）——的公民，从这危险中醒来。他们在这桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）里看到了更糟之事的（先兆预兆/harbinger)：民主从内部缓慢的（血管脉络般的/vascular）收窄。一个（风向标般具指标意义的/bellwether）选区，长久以来一直是阴谋者们一份（特别的/particular）猎物，却踊跃投票、把这个共和国（导引/steer）回公平的划界。这桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）的企图，因一个阴谋者们无法（破解/decipher）的讽刺，反倒成了那个重新唤起一个昏昏欲睡之选民群体的（提醒/reminder)。

这补救是程序性的，而非复仇性的。这个共和国没有向（惩罚报应/retribution）的诱惑（屈服投降/surrender)；它没有把阴谋者们关进监狱、或把他们（弄成/render）弃儿。它只是废止了那张腐败的地图、并把一条新规则牢固确立下来：边界今后将由一个独立机构来划定，置于任何派系（钱柜/coffer）的触及之外。这桩（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）被解除了；阴谋者们事业的（残余/remainder）在日光下枯萎。那（伪造者/forger）的地图作为一件（纪念物/memento）进了档案——一则（火绒般/tinder）干燥的警示，警示着公平投票那洁净（圆周般周正的/circular）几何是何等容易被（损毁/mar)。

这场政治（纠纷乱局/imbroglio）之外，寻常生活保持着它（灵活柔韧的/limber)、（蜿蜒迂回的/meander）步调。一个（采集觅食者/forager）在（针叶树/conifer）林子里采集一颗（块茎/tuber）和野生的（花蜜/nectar)；一个（沐浴者/bather）在那（含水层/aquifer）滋养的清凉泉水里游泳；一只（獾/badger）和一条（毛毛虫/caterpillar）与一只好奇的（公鹅/gander）共享着树篱。在市集上，一个小贩在一个（研钵/mortar）里搅着汤、用一个（滤器/colander）滤它；一个匠人弯折着（木材/timber)、（焊接/solder）着一个铜（圆筒/cylinder)；一个（护林员/ranger）从山间小路上滚开一块（巨砾/boulder)。那（暮色微光的/crepuscular）光线映照着一根（大梁/girder）上霜的（极地般/polar）闪光；一（罐/pitcher）（姜/ginger）汁啤酒从一个（肩膀/shoulder）传到另一个（肩膀/shoulder)；一个老（弓箭手/archer）教一个孩子把一支箭（导引瞄准/steer）准。公众肌体里没有恐惧的（溃疡/ulcer)，只有一个自由民族稳定的（血管脉络般的/vascular）脉搏。

这桩插曲作为一种（特别的/particular）教训，载入了民族（准则典籍/canon)。史家写道：一个共和国，受到威胁的不只来自（壮观惊人的/spectacular）（政变/coup）或（神谕般晦涩的/oracular）蛊惑民心者；它也能被那悄无声息的（操纵选区划分/gerrymander）、地图里的（密码/cipher)、趁公民们（沉睡/slumber）时划下的那（伪造者/forger）的线条所掏空。自由的代价是一种（目力眼睛般的/ocular)、乃至（耳朵般倾听的/auricular）警觉——那份去（破解/decipher）权力之（行话/vernacular)、并从一个（毛毛虫/caterpillar）形状的选区中（推断/infer）出其下（血管脉络般的/vascular）威胁的意愿。（搁置推延/defer）这样的审视、或在公民职责上（装病偷懒/malinger)，便是在招致自治的缓慢（交出投降/surrender)。

于是韦尔莫利亚，自由了一百四十五载，领悟到：一个民主政体的廉正，活在它最不（壮观/spectacular）的细节之中——一张地图上那条诚实的线、一位拒绝（伪造/forge）之（制图师/cartographer）那（持重的/sober）工作、一个不肯（沉睡/slumber）之公众的（反驳回应/rejoinder)。元帅靠（密码/cipher）和（伪造者/forger）的笔来统治、靠对真相本身的（操纵歪曲/gerrymander)；他的国家，在他倒台一个半世纪之后，选择了那更艰难的公平（行话方言/vernacular)——按地理、而非按贪婪去划它那（周正的/circular）线条、（破解/decipher）每一桩（神谕般晦涩的/oracular）欺骗、并在它种种制度那（世俗的/secular）（支柱/pillar）之下，守住那一条（特别的/particular）（提醒/reminder)：没有哪张地图，无论划得多么巧妙，能够长久地（拖累羁绊/encumber）一个决心要（导引/steer）自己航向的民族。

本批词根亮点：

• -ary/-ory 结尾大集合：seminary（播种知识处）/luminary（发光者）/mortuary（死亡之所）/refectory（恢复体力处）

• cemetery：来自希腊语"睡觉的地方"（koimeterion），墓地=长眠之处

• tawdry：来自 St Audrey（圣奥德里节），集市上出售的廉价花边蕾丝，后变成"俗丽"的形容词

• refectory：来自拉丁语"恢复体力"（reficere），食堂=恢复体力的地方

• olfactory/gustatory：嗅觉/味觉，感官系统的拉丁词根对

• effrontery：ef（去除）+ frons（额头），没有脸=厚颜无耻

• cavalry/chivalry：都来自拉丁 caballus（马），cavalier/cavalcade 同族

quiz.question: _____ pillar
quiz.explanation: 柱子; 支柱, 石柱. The ancient temple was supported by a massive stone pillar. 古老的寺庙由一根巨大的石柱支撑。 | pila->柱（拉丁），pillar->支撑柱（cf. pillow枕头，compile编辑=堆积在一起） || 文化联想：中国古寺里的粗大石柱最适合帮助记忆 pillar，可以说 **a stone pillar — “An ancient Chinese temple may be supported by a massive stone pillar carved from a single block.”**

quiz.question: caterpillar _____
quiz.explanation: 毛毛虫; 履带, 履带. The tank moved slowly on its caterpillar track across rough terrain. 坦克在崎岖的地形上用履带缓慢移动。 | chate->毛，pillier->毛发（古法语），caterpillar->毛茸茸的虫=毛毛虫 || 文化联想：中国军事博物馆里的坦克履带最适合帮助记忆 caterpillar，可以说 **a caterpillar track — “A tank displayed in a military museum moves on a caterpillar track designed to grip rough ground.”**

quiz.question: _____ collar
quiz.explanation: 衣领; 项圈, 白领. She worked in a white collar office environment. 她在白领办公环境中工作。 | collum->颈（拉丁），collar->围绕颈部的=衣领（white collar白领，blue collar蓝领） || 文化联想：中文“白领”最适合帮助记忆 collar，可以说 **a white-collar worker — “An office employee in Shanghai may be described as a white-collar worker because the term collar is associated with office work.”**

quiz.question: molar _____
quiz.explanation: 臼齿, 臼齿. The dentist examined my molar tooth for cavities. 牙医检查我的臼齿是否有蛀牙。 | mola->磨石（拉丁），molar->像磨石一样研磨的牙=臼齿（cf. molecule分子，grind磨碎） || 文化联想：中国牙科诊所检查后槽牙最适合帮助记忆 molar，可以说 **a molar tooth — “A dentist may find a cavity in a molar tooth at the back of a patient’s mouth.”**

quiz.question: polar ________
quiz.explanation: 极地的; 截然相反的, 截然相反. Their political views were polar opposite on every issue. 他们的政治观点在每个问题上都截然相反。 | polus->极点（希腊），polar->极点的（cf. pole极点，bipolar两极的） || 文化联想：中文“截然相反”最适合帮助记忆 polar，可以说 **polar opposites — “Two proposals that differ on every major point may be described as polar opposites.”**

quiz.question: ______ vernacular
quiz.explanation: 方言; 本地话, 街头俚语. The rapper used street vernacular in his lyrics. 说唱歌手在歌词中使用街头俚语。 | verna->家生奴隶（拉丁，在家出生的），vernacular->家乡原生的语言=方言（cf. vernal春天的） || 文化联想：北京话、四川话等本地口语最适合帮助记忆 vernacular，可以说 **local vernacular — “A novelist may use the local vernacular of Beijing to make dialogue sound natural and rooted in place.”**

quiz.question: oracular _____________
quiz.explanation: 神谕的; 晦涩的, 神谕般的声明. The philosopher made an oracular pronouncement about the future. 哲学家对未来作出了神谕般的声明。 | oraculum->神谕（拉丁，来自os->口），oracular->像神谕一样晦涩=神谕的（cf. oracle神谕，oration演讲） || 文化联想：中文“像算命先生一样说得玄乎”最适合帮助记忆 oracular，可以说 **an oracular pronouncement — “A fortune-teller who speaks in mysterious, ambiguous phrases may sound as though making an oracular pronouncement.”**

quiz.question: spectacular ____
quiz.explanation: 壮观的; 惊人的, 壮观的景色. quiz.question: _______ forger
quiz.explanation: 伪造者, 技艺高超的伪造者. The skilled forger created convincing fake documents. 技艺高超的伪造者制作了令人信服的假文件。 | forge->锻造/伪造（拉丁fabricare），forger->锻造者/伪造者（cf. fabricate制造/编造，falsify伪造） || 文化联想：中国古玩市场里的假证书、假字画最适合帮助记忆 forger，可以说 **a skilled forger — “A skilled forger may imitate an old seal or signature closely enough to deceive an inexperienced buyer.”**

quiz.question: ___ __ auger
quiz.explanation: 螺旋钻, 使用螺旋钻. The carpenter will use an auger to drill holes in the wood. 木匠将使用螺旋钻在木头上钻孔。 | nafu->hub of wheel（古英语，车轮毂），auger->从nafu+gar（矛）演变，用于钻孔的螺旋工具（注意来自a+nauger） || 文化联想：传统木匠用螺旋钻在木料上打孔最适合帮助记忆 auger，可以说 **use an auger — “A carpenter may use an auger to bore a clean hole through a thick wooden beam.”**

quiz.question: archer ____
quiz.explanation: 弓箭手, 射水鱼. The archer fish shoots water at insects above the surface. 射水鱼向水面上的昆虫射水。 | arc->弓（拉丁arcus），archer->使用弓的人=弓箭手（cf. arc弧，archery射箭，arcade拱廊） || 文化联想：中国水族馆里的射水鱼最适合帮助记忆 archer，可以说 **an archer fish — “An archer fish can shoot a jet of water at an insect resting above the surface.”**

quiz.question: pitcher _____
quiz.explanation: 水罐; 投手, 猪笼草. The carnivorous pitcher plant traps insects for nutrition. 食肉的猪笼草捕捉昆虫作为营养。 | pitcher->水罐（古法语pichier），pitcher plant->形似水罐的植物=猪笼草（cf. pitch投掷，pitcher投手/水罐） || 文化联想：中国植物园里的猪笼草最适合帮助记忆 pitcher，可以说 **a pitcher plant — “A pitcher plant traps insects inside a deep, slippery leaf structure filled with digestive fluid.”**

quiz.question: lexicographer ___
quiz.explanation: 词典编纂者, 词典编纂者的工作. The lexicographer job requires extensive knowledge of language. 词典编纂者的工作需要广泛的语言知识。 | lexis->词语，grapher->书写者，lexicographer->书写词语的人=词典编纂者（cf. lexicon词典，geography地理） || 文化联想：《现代汉语词典》的编纂工作最适合帮助记忆 lexicographer，可以说 **a professional lexicographer — “A professional lexicographer may spend years collecting examples and refining definitions for a major Chinese dictionary.”**

quiz.question: cartographer's ___
quiz.explanation: 地图制作者, 地图制作者的地图. The cartographer's map showed incredible detail of the terrain. 地图制作者的地图显示了地形的惊人细节。 | carta->纸/地图（拉丁），grapher->书写者，cartographer->绘制地图的人（cf. chart图表，graphic图形） || 文化联想：中国古代地图和现代测绘都需要制图师，最适合帮助记忆 cartographer，可以说 **a cartographer's map — “A cartographer's map of a mountain region may combine elevation, rivers, roads, and place names with great precision.”**

quiz.question: ______ cipher
quiz.explanation: 密码; 暗号, 秘密密码. Spies communicated using a secret cipher during the war. 间谍在战争期间使用秘密密码进行通信。 | sifr->零（阿拉伯语，来自梵语sunya->空），cipher->零/密码（cf. zero零，decipher解密） || 文化联想：抗战题材故事中的秘密暗号最适合帮助记忆 cipher，可以说 **a secret cipher — “In a wartime spy story, agents may exchange messages written in a secret cipher that outsiders cannot read.”**

quiz.question: decipher _ ____
quiz.explanation: 破译; 解码, 破译密码. The cryptographer worked to decipher a code from the enemy. 密码学家努力破译敌人的密码。 | de->去除，cipher->密码，decipher->去除密码的遮掩=破译（cf. encipher加密，cipher密码） || 文化联想：中文“破译密码”最适合帮助记忆 decipher，可以说 **decipher a code — “A cryptanalyst may spend hours trying to decipher a code hidden in an intercepted message.”**

quiz.question: encipher _ _______
quiz.explanation: 加密, 加密信息. Intelligence officers must encipher a message before transmission. 情报官员必须在传输前加密信息。 | en->使成为，cipher->密码，encipher->使成为密码=加密（cf. decipher破译，encrypt加密） || 文化联想：中文“把情报加密后再发送”最适合帮助记忆 encipher，可以说 **encipher a message — “An intelligence officer may encipher a message before transmitting it over an insecure channel.”**

quiz.question: ___ gusher
quiz.explanation: 喷涌的东西, 油井喷涌. The prospectors struck an oil gusher in the Texas plains. 勘探者在德克萨斯平原上发现了一个喷油井。 | gush->喷涌（古挪威gjósa），gusher->喷涌的东西=喷油井/过分热情的人（cf. gust一阵风，gust of enthusiasm热情迸发） || 文化联想：gusher 常用于喷涌的油井，可用中国石油勘探史里的喷油场景来记忆，可以说 **an oil gusher — “During early oil exploration, striking a highly pressurized reservoir could produce an oil gusher that sprayed crude high into the air.”**

quiz.question: ______ bather
quiz.explanation: 沐浴者, 公共泳者. The public bather enjoyed swimming at the community pool. 公共泳者喜欢在社区游泳池游泳。 | bath->沐浴（古英语bæth），bather->沐浴者（cf. bath浴室，bathe沐浴，bathroom浴室） || 文化联想：中国公共泳池里的游泳者最适合帮助记忆 bather，可以说 **a public bather — “A public bather at a community pool should shower first and follow the posted hygiene rules.”**

quiz.question: bellwether _____
quiz.explanation: 领头羊; 指标, 指标股. Analysts watch the bellwether stock to predict market trends. 分析师关注指标股以预测市场趋势。 | bell->铃铛，wether->阉割的公羊，bellwether->脖子上挂铃铛领路的公羊=先驱/指标（cf. whether是否，weather天气） || 文化联想：中文“风向标、领头羊”最适合帮助记忆 bellwether，可以说 **a market bellwether — “A large technology company can become a market bellwether whose results influence expectations for the broader sector.”**
